meta.source: btprod_2026-04-28.bak (3.0 GB native SQL Server backup) restored to Docker SQL Server 2022; INFORMATION_SCHEMA + sys catalogs dumped via restore_and_dump.sh; consumed here via verified Phase 0 extracts only
limitations: Raw 3.0 GB .bak is NOT in this workspace; nothing here was re-verified against the database, all figures come from the Phase 0 verified extracts listed in inputs.

SchemaInventory.md lists only the top 34 tables by row count; the remaining 1,206 table rows live in the source xlsx, which is also not in this workspace. Per-table detail below is therefore complete for large tables and notes-derived for the rest.
Only 100 of 1,885 stored-procedure bodies were extracted in Phase 0 (high-risk subsystems); business logic in the remaining ~1,785 procs is uncharacterized.
Schema is single-schema dbo, pure PascalCase, no prefixes.

migration_priority_legend.M1-M3-prep: Prerequisite cleanup/build before the migration month (A-18 UDF promotion M1-W2; WS1 catalog + UoM cleanup and WS7 cruft exclusion recommended to start M3/Aug)
migration_priority_legend.M4-W14: Month 4 wave 1 (Sep, 'Migration V1'): ETL pipeline build, financial + master data migration, Dry Run #1
migration_priority_legend.M4-W15: Month 4 EDI wave: Tier 1 vendor EDI setup + UAT (partner re-setup, not row ETL)
migration_priority_legend.M4-W16: Month 4 wave 2 (Sep, 'Migration V2'): open documents, COD gate, approval workflows, Dry Run #2
migration_priority_legend.M6-W21: Month 6 cutover wave (Nov): final production ETL run on frozen BisTrack snapshot
migration_priority_legend.seed-not-migrate: Rebuilt or seeded natively in HardscapeOS; no row migration from BisTrack
migration_priority_legend.no-migrate: Excluded: empty subsystem, cruft, or reference-only history kept in the read-only BisTrack archive
migration_priority_legend.triage: Unclassified; needs G2 triage before a wave can be assigned

domain_mappings.transformation_notes: Migrate 8,485 customers minus dead/duplicate accounts; EXCLUDE the 8,408-row Customer_BAK_241031 copy (a blind union would near-double the customer base). AR opening balances computed per customer, not by replaying 11.67M CustomerBalanceHistory rows (archive those). Credit-hold columns carry 1:1 onto the customer record; gating behavior is pending P1. M9 sync: customer master = native post-fork (push on edit, hourly pull for net-new); bistrack_id_map provides BisTrack ID <-> native UUID identity.

domain_mappings.hardscapeos_domain: product (catalog, categories, facets, UoM) + inventory (reorder points)
domain_mappings.transformation_notes: 189-column Product flattens to products + promoted hardscape facets (migration 051); ProductGroup hierarchy maps to product_categories with hardscape facet assignment. 'Per' system: Per (1,454 rows, ConversionToBase + BasePer flag) maps to the expanded UoM enum (052: PLT/TON/LYR/PC/CYD) + conversion table, but PerConversion has only 42 product-level rows for 4,779 products, with ~7,257 rows in PerRule/PerRuleConversion that may encode rule-based conversions; resolve which mechanism is authoritative, then bulk-seed factors (WS1 gate). Substitution self-FKs (ReplacementID/ParentID/SellProductID) map to explicit product-relationship records (feeds quote comparison, Active #6). 50-60 live UDF fields promote from the 1-column OrderLineUDF blob (A-18, M1-W2). Derive is_active from StockTransaction recency + OrderLine activity, no source flag exists. M9 sync: product = BisTrack master until cutover, hourly pull.

BisTrack stores quotes and orders as one 241-column OrderHeader differentiated by OrderType + status, G2 must explicitly decide unified-with-type vs split quote/order entities; either way the migration filter is OrderType, never the empty Quote tables. Quote lifecycle columns (FollowUpDateTime, ExpiryDate, QuoteRank, DateTimeQuoteAccepted/Rejected, CPQQuoteID) feed follow-up automation (Active #2) and quote delivery (Active #9). IsReservation + DaysToReserve map to parked-order state (Active #4). OrderLine (187 cols) + OrderLinePriceInfo (87 cols) collapse into a normalized line + price breakdown. Migrate OPEN documents only (WS4): non-invoiced orders, parked orders, active quotes; each open line recreates its allocation. M9 sync: orders native-always; BisTrack-originated post-fork orders surface as missing_target.

domain_mappings.hardscapeos_domain: inventory (on-hand, allocations, cost layers, cycle counts, replenishment)
domain_mappings.transformation_notes: Confirm valuation method (FIFO vs weighted-average vs standard) FIRST, it decides whether 3.97M StockValuationData rows collapse to average cost or prune to active layers (remaining qty > 0). Fold StockReceiptCost landed costs (freight/duty/handling) into layers or separate landed-cost records (A-16). Resolve negative on-hand balances and stale allocations BEFORE snapshot; migrate allocations only for still-open orders and reconcile against StockAllocation totals. Reorder points / lead times / preferred vendors from ProductBranchSupplier seed the replenishment engine (A-12); velocity seeds from SalesAnalysis2 + ProductAnalysis. Acceptance: valuation matches within 0.1% / $100 vs rpt2201; zero negative balances; final snapshot in M6-W21 freeze window with physical count (WS6).

OrderPayment.CashOnDeliveryPayment is today an informational per-payment bit, HardscapeOS PROMOTES it to an enforced state-machine gate (Active #3, M4-W16) driven by PaymentTerms + customer credit state. OrderHeader.PaymentTermsID FK confirmed (header-fragment ambiguity resolved: PaymentTermsID, not PaymentType), crosswalk terms to native payment_terms. Open payments on open orders migrate with their documents; settled payment history archives. Bank-rec ownership (native vs Great Plains, Moneris/EFT/cheque matching back to OrderPayment rows) is an open A-01/A-02 discovery question.

domain_mappings.hardscapeos_domain: finance (native GL: gl_accounts, gl_journal_entries, gl_journal_lines; GP export adapter)
domain_mappings.transformation_notes: Dibbits' third-party GL is Microsoft Dynamics GP (Great Plains), confirmed 2026-05-19. Dual-track A-01: Track 1 (cutover-blocking) reverse-engineers the BisTrack->GP posting contract from GLExport + GeneralLedgerExportLine (46 cols) + AccountsInvoiceExportLine (62 cols) so every HardscapeOS transaction lands in GP in the same shape and month-end close runs unchanged; Track 2 builds the native GL in parallel so GP can be deprecated on Dibbits' timeline. GLExportRule's 386,815 rows (transaction-scale for a 'rule' table) must be explained, likely per-transaction mapping/staging; the answer probably lives in unextracted stored procedures. Migrate chart-of-accounts mapping + opening balances + open AR/AP only; 572K GeneralLedger journal rows stay in the archive. GP mechanism/version/posting depth = open discovery.

Do NOT migrate the 3M-row Audit trail into audit_log, keep BisTrack as a read-only archive for 12 months and start the native A-21 audit trail fresh at cutover. LockHold's polymorphic lock (TransactionID + TransactionType + LockedBy/ClearedBy + timestamps) is the proven pattern to generalize for Active #10 post-pick change control (ChangeRequest, ApprovalChain, DelegationRule) and A-26 approval workflows; active locks at cutover are transient state, re-establish, don't ETL. Discrepancy resolutions during parallel-op also write to audit_log (M9 zero-trust checklist).

Open/unpaid invoices migrate as line-level AR opening detail (feeds CP-05 portal invoice pay and statements); paid history stays in the archive, retrievable for 12 months. Invoice totals must tie to AR opening balances and to the GP seam.

Journey* tables are the real dispatch system (9,596 journeys); the 30-table Delivery/Dispatch subsystem holds only 64 rows and must not shape the target model. PROMOTE the four rptJourneyManifest* views into first-class Manifest + ManifestVersion entities and ADD MTO classification fields (Active #1). JourneyLine/JourneyStop double as load tickets (P3), no separate LoadTicket entity needed. Hand-seed the 11-vehicle/11-driver fleet; migrate only open journeys at M6-W21; lookup masters (DeliveryTime/DeliveryOption/DeliveryArea) crosswalk as config since OrderHeader FKs them.

bistrack_tables: Customer (OnHold, NeverPutOrdersOnHold, CreditApprovalRequired, CreditControlStatusID, CreditRatingID, NumberOfOrders...)
domain_mappings.transformation_notes: Reuse credit fields 1:1 on the customer record with lookup crosswalks. The enforcement behavior (when holds block order entry/dispatch) is pending P1, NOT YET DISCUSSED with Dibbits. COD enforcement (Active #3) reads this same credit state, so the P1 decision should precede the W16 COD gate build.

bistrack_tables: (28 EDI tables, ~122K rows; not enumerated in extract fragment)
domain_mappings.transformation_notes: EDI is live at Dibbits. Re-onboard Tier 1 vendors natively (A-11, M4-W15) with UAT per partner; historical EDI documents archive. Enumerate the 28 tables in the next extract pass to identify partner configs vs document logs.

bistrack_tables: (56 price-list tables; not enumerated in extract fragment)
domain_mappings.transformation_notes: Price-list-driven: migrate current/effective price lists with the catalog (M4-W14); the A-07 Pricing Configurator (M1-W3) owns rule mechanics natively. ProductPriceHistory2 (463,668 rows, note the '2' version suffix, verify it is the authoritative copy) archives; A-08 Price Change Log starts fresh. OrderLinePriceInfo's 87-column breakdown defines the pricing-trace fields quoting must preserve.

anomalies.finding: UoM conversion coverage gap: PerConversion holds 42 rows against 4,779 products (Per master: 1,454 UoMs). UoM auto-conversion, the core selling motion for hardscape (pallet <-> piece <-> sq-ft <-> ton), fails for virtually the entire catalog without massive seeding.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory.md Cover ('CRITICAL DATA-QUALITY FLAGS: PerConversion has only 42 rows for 4,779 products') + Subsystem Summary ('Per (1,454) + PerConversion (only 42 rows!) ... SEVERE coverage gap'); BiTrackMapping row 8 rated High risk; Inventory-Migration WS1 makes UoM normalization a gate that 'blocks everything'. Nuance: Per-subsystem total is 8,753 rows, implying ~7,257 rows in PerRule/PerRuleConversion, rule-based conversion may carry part of the real logic and must be characterized before sizing the seeding effort.
anomalies.recommended_action: G2: characterize PerRule/PerRuleConversion semantics (and the relevant proc bodies) to determine true coverage; then execute the WS1 seeding plan, bulk import tool + AI-assisted factor population + admin audit UI (Active #8), with the acceptance gate 'every active product has a base UoM and >=1 selling UoM with a verified factor' BEFORE catalog migration (M4-W14). Start no later than M3.

anomalies.finding: Inventory valuation method (FIFO vs weighted-average vs standard cost) is unconfirmed with Dibbits, yet it dictates the entire cost-layer migration design (WS3, the hardest workstream).
anomalies.evidence: Inventory-Migration WS3 ('Valuation method confirmation, confirm with Dibbits... determines whether we migrate individual cost layers or collapse to a single average cost') and Open Question #1.
anomalies.recommended_action: Get the answer from Amanda (financials SME) before G2 freezes the inventory cost model; design the cost-layer schema to support both layer-based and average costing if the answer slips.

anomalies.finding: StockValuationData is 3,973,238 rows of FIFO cost-layer history, most of it presumably fully consumed layers; migrating it wholesale is infeasible and unnecessary, but the pruning rule and history-retention depth are undecided.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables row 2 (3,973,238 rows, 12 cols); Inventory-Migration WS3 ('migrate only the active cost layers (remaining quantity > 0)'; historical cost options a/b/c undecided).
anomalies.recommended_action: Prune to active layers; reconcile total valuation vs rpt2201BusinessAdvisorProductValuation within $100 and 0.1%; get owner sign-off on history depth (recommend: active layers only, full history in read-only archive).

anomalies.finding: Negative stock balances are expected in BisTrack (mis-sequenced transactions accumulate them) and cannot be migrated; volume at Dibbits is unquantified.
anomalies.evidence: Inventory-Migration WS2 ('BisTrack systems commonly accumulate negative stock balances... you can't migrate a -47 pallet count'); WS2 acceptance requires zero negative balances in target.
anomalies.recommended_action: Run a negative-balance scan in the next extract pass to quantify; resolve every negative in BisTrack before snapshot (adjustment policy needs ops sign-off); pair with the WS6 pre-cutover physical count.

anomalies.finding: Product has no clean IsActive flag, so the active-vs-dead split of 4,779 SKUs (the very first migration filter) must be inferred, and duplicate SKUs are expected from organic growth.
anomalies.evidence: Inventory-Migration WS1 ('BisTrack has no clean IsActive flag, requires cross-referencing StockTransaction recency and OrderLine activity'; duplicate detection called out).
anomalies.recommended_action: Define the activity heuristic (e.g., stock movement or order line within trailing 24 months OR on-hand > 0), produce the candidate dead-SKU list, and have Ryan B. (inventory SMEs) ratify it; flag-don't-delete discontinued SKUs for historical order reference.

anomalies.finding: 168,395 OrderLineUDF rows sit in a 1-column table (opaque packed/blob UDF storage) holding 50-60 actively used business fields (manufacturer, collection, finish, color, coverage) that must become first-class product columns before any catalog or inventory migration.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables row 15 (OrderLineUDF, 1 column, 168,395 rows); Inventory-Migration WS1 attribute promotion ('scoped as A-18 but must complete BEFORE inventory migration').
anomalies.recommended_action: A-18 ETL (scheduled M1-W2): parse the UDF payload format, inventory the distinct fields, confirm the 50-60 live-field list with Dibbits, promote to migration-051 facet columns; treat unparsed remainders as metadata JSONB.

anomalies.finding: 1,885 stored procedures exist but only 100 bodies were extracted; business rules for GL export shaping, COD/credit behavior, stock costing, and locking may live in the ~1,785 unexamined procs.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Cover ('Stored procedures 1,885; Procs body extracted 100 (matching high-risk subsystems)').
anomalies.recommended_action: Targeted second extraction pass during G2 keyed to open questions: GLExport*/GP posting procs, OrderPayment/COD procs, StockValuation costing procs, LockHold lifecycle procs, PerRule conversion procs. Do not finalize the finance or inventory data model on table shapes alone.

anomalies.finding: M9 bi-directional sync architecture assumes WebTrack supports incremental queries (?since= / ?modified_since=), which is still unverified; without it, every 15-minute cycle becomes a full-table pull.
anomalies.evidence: m9-bistrack-sync.md Critical Assumption #2 ('needs verification. [Validate by: code spike, open]') and top risk ('WebTrack API has undocumented quirks, High/High').
anomalies.recommended_action: Run the code spike against a WebTrack sandbox in week 1 of M9 work (M2-W8 per roadmap); if unsupported, fall back to full-pull + local diffing at a reduced cadence and re-size the sync budget. CSV export/import is the documented last resort.

anomalies.finding: 626 of 1,240 tables (50.5%, ~1.1M rows) are bucketed as 'Other', unclassified, and demonstrably include operational data: Permission (218,448 rows), SalesAnalysis2/3 (170K/167K), ScanTrackImage (125,534), rpt2201 valuation snapshot (68,956). The migration surface is not fully mapped.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Subsystem Summary ('Other | 626 | 1106720') + All Tables rows 8, 11, 16, 25, 31.
anomalies.recommended_action: G2 classification pass over the full 1,240-table list (needs the source xlsx or a re-dump): bucket by row count > 0 and FK proximity to mapped subsystems; explicitly disposition every table with > 1,000 rows. Until then, treat subsystem totals as floors, not ceilings.

anomalies.finding: Customer_BAK_241031, an 8,408-row backup copy of Customer from 2024-10-31, sits in production. Blind schema-walk migration would nearly double the customer base with 7-month-stale duplicates; its presence also signals ad-hoc DBA table copies elsewhere.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Cover critical flag ('Customer_BAK_241031 (8,408 rows), 2024-10-31 customer backup table left in production. Audit before...'); live Customer = 8,485 rows (delta of 77 customers since the backup). Inventory-Migration WS7: 'Do NOT migrate.'
anomalies.recommended_action: Add to the hard exclusion list; diff against live Customer once as a cheap data-quality audit (the 77-row delta bounds churn since Oct 2024); sweep the full table list for other *_BAK / date-suffixed copies and exclude them all.

anomalies.finding: PickingNoteHeader has 0 rows, the entire Pick subsystem (8 tables, including PickingNoteLine, PickingNoteItem, OrderPickingHistory, HandheldPickingNoteLine) is unused at Dibbits.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Cover flag + Subsystem Summary ('Pick | 8 | 0'); BiTrackMapping row 7 ('PickingNoteHeader (0 ROWS, UNUSED)').

anomalies.finding: ProductPack has 0 rows, pallet/pack tracking (8 tables) is unused, despite pallets being the physical core of a hardscape yard.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Cover flag + Subsystem Summary ('Pack | 8 | 0, pallet tracking not currently used').
anomalies.recommended_action: Treat Active #7 pallet/load tracking as net-new capability with no legacy data: PalletScan/LoaderConfirm/DiscrepancyFlag designed fresh; pallet_count on products comes from promoted UDF attributes, not Pack tables.

anomalies.finding: The 30-table Delivery/Dispatch subsystem holds 64 total rows, effectively empty, while real dispatch runs through Journey/Manifest (JourneyHeader 9,596 rows). The obvious-looking tables are the wrong model to copy.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Subsystem Summary ('Delivery / Dispatch | 30 | 64' vs 'Journey / Manifest | 21 | 34,962'); BiTrackMapping P2/P3 point at Delivery + Journey tables jointly.
anomalies.recommended_action: Model HardscapeOS logistics on Journey*/JourneyStop semantics; carry over only the Delivery* lookup masters (DeliveryTime/DeliveryOption/DeliveryArea) that OrderHeader FKs; confirm with Dibbits why delivery notes are unused (likely superseded by journey paperwork).

anomalies.finding: Manifest infrastructure exists only as 4 report views (rptJourneyManifestHeader/Pack/NALine/RB...), not physical tables, there is no persisted manifest entity to migrate or version, yet MTO compliance (Active #1) requires durable, versioned manifests.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Cover ('Manifest infrastructure EXISTS as 4 views'); BiTrackMapping row 1 ('PROMOTE the four manifest views to first-class objects (Manifest, ManifestVersion). ADD MTOClassi...').
anomalies.recommended_action: G2: design Manifest + ManifestVersion as first-class tables with MTO classification fields; extract the 4 view definitions in the next pass so the projection logic (what BisTrack considers a manifest line/pack) is reproduced exactly.

anomalies.finding: Internal inconsistency in the extract: the Payment subsystem reports 25 tables / 166 total rows, yet its own note (and the scope mapping) cite OrderPayment at 40,954 rows, OrderPayment is evidently classified under Order. Subsystem totals cannot be trusted as table-location guides for COD work.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Subsystem Summary ('Payment | 25 | 166 | OrderPayment (40,954 rows). CashOnDeliveryPayment bit lives here.'); same pattern: ProductPriceHistory2 (464K) cited in the Pricing note but classified under Product/Item (All Tables row 5).
anomalies.recommended_action: Treat subsystem assignment as advisory; resolve every key table's real identity from the full table list during G2. For COD (Active #3, M4-W16), source from OrderPayment regardless of bucket.

anomalies.finding: Extreme table width at the heart of the migration: OrderHeader 241 columns, OrderLine 187, AccountsInvoiceExportLine 62, OrderLinePriceInfo 87, Product 189. The order/quote mapping alone covers ~600 columns of denormalized state.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables rows 13, 14, 9, 34 and Subsystem Summary (Product 189 cols).
anomalies.recommended_action: Budget G2 mapping time accordingly; produce a column-level disposition sheet (map / derive / drop / archive) for OrderHeader + OrderLine before writing ETL; the verified header fragment proves real column widths must come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA, not proc signatures.

anomalies.finding: StockAllocation (66,930 rows) likely contains stale allocations against orders cancelled, expired, or fulfilled years ago; migrating them would corrupt available-to-sell math from day 1.
anomalies.evidence: Inventory-Migration WS7 ('likely contains allocations against orders that were cancelled, expired, or fulfilled years ago') and WS4 reconciliation requirement.
anomalies.recommended_action: Migrate only allocations whose parent order is open/non-invoiced; reconcile allocated-quantity-per-product between systems as a WS4 acceptance gate (available-to-sell must match).

anomalies.finding: Inventory migration is 66-96 hours across 7 interdependent workstreams, but the master plan carried it as a single ~2-week 'Migration Script V1' line item; the cleanup prerequisites (WS1/WS7) must start in M3 (Aug), a month with no migration budget.
anomalies.evidence: Inventory-Migration effort summary + IMPORTANT callout ('cannot fit into 2 weeks alongside other feature work... starting in Month 3 (August)'); roadmap.yaml M4 W14/W16 are the only migration weeks.
anomalies.recommended_action: Commander decision: pull WS1 (catalog/UoM cleanup) and WS7 (exclusion lists) forward into M3 alongside W9-W12 feature work, or accept right-shift risk to the M4 gate ('Dry Run #2 data integrity >98%'). Reflect in the Master Checklist.

anomalies.finding: ScanTrackImage holds 125,534 rows x 24 columns, almost certainly scanned document/image payloads (PODs, signatures, tickets) stored in-database. Unaddressed, this is a silent multi-GB blob migration with retention/legal implications; ignored, it strands delivery evidence.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables row 25; table is bucketed 'Other' and appears in no workstream.
anomalies.recommended_action: Characterize in the next extract pass (column types, avg payload size, linkage to orders/journeys); decide: migrate to object storage, keep in read-only archive with a lookup link from HardscapeOS, or drop. Retention requirement needs Dibbits input.

anomalies.finding: GLExportRule contains 386,815 rows, transaction-scale volume for a table named like configuration. The BisTrack->Great Plains posting mechanism is not understood at the level required to reproduce it on Day 1 (which is cutover-blocking under dual-track A-01).
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables row 6 (GLExportRule, 7 cols, 386,815 rows) alongside GLExport (181,249) and GeneralLedgerExportLine (165,838); A-01 confirms GP integration mechanism/posting depth still open discovery.
anomalies.recommended_action: Prioritize GL export procs in the BT-A-007 extraction pass; sample GLExportRule rows to determine whether it is per-transaction account mapping, staging, or log; schedule the A-01 GP walkthrough (mechanism: eConnect/Integration Manager/flat file; summary vs detail) with Amanda before G2 finance modeling closes.

anomalies.finding: CustomerBalanceHistory is 11,665,740 rows (3 columns), the largest table in the database, but is balance history, not open AR; wholesale migration would dominate ETL runtime for no operational value.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables row 1; Customer subsystem note ('11.6M-row CustomerBalanceHistory').
anomalies.recommended_action: Compute AR opening balances per customer at snapshot time; leave the history in the read-only archive. Confirm with Amanda how much balance/statement history the finance team needs queryable post-cutover.

anomalies.finding: The central Audit table holds 2,999,981 rows (plus AuditDetailChar/Num/Type/Group satellites; subsystem total 3.21M). Migrating it would pollute the native audit_log and bloat the cutover; not retaining access to it loses the compliance trail.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables row 3 + Subsystem Summary (Audit 13 tables / 3,214,953 rows); Inventory-Migration WS7 ('reference-only, don't migrate... keep BisTrack accessible as a read-only archive for 12 months post-cutover').
anomalies.recommended_action: Do not migrate; stand up the read-only BisTrack archive (already implied by the M6-W24 decommission-confirmation gate) and get Dibbits' written agreement on the 12-month retention window.

anomalies.finding: Six operational unknowns that shape the G2 inventory/locations model and the cutover runbook are still unanswered: valuation method, bin-level vs branch-level tracking, lot/serial tracking, transaction-history depth, freeze-window tolerance, and last-physical-count recency.
anomalies.evidence: Inventory-Migration 'Open Questions for Dibbits' #1-#6.
anomalies.recommended_action: Put all six on the next SME breakaway call (Amanda for #1; Ryan B. for #2/#3/#6; ops for #4/#5); G2 should not freeze the locations/lot model before #2 and #3 are answered.

anomalies.finding: RESOLVED: column widths read from the .bak header fragment were stored-procedure parameter widths, not real column widths (e.g., DeliveryPostCode appeared varchar(5); real column is varchar(50), Canadian postal codes fit). Cross-cutting risk C2 closed.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory 'Verified Header Fragment' table (all 9 rows verified against the restore; PaymentTermsID identity also confirmed there).
anomalies.recommended_action: None, closed. Process rule going forward: only INFORMATION_SCHEMA widths from the verified dump are authoritative.

anomalies.finding: Quote subsystem tables (QuoteRank, ItemQuoteStatus, +1) hold 0 data rows, they are tracking lookups; real quotes are OrderHeader rows. Any tool that 'migrates quotes' from Quote tables migrates nothing.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Cover ('Quotes are NOT separate tables') + Subsystem Summary ('Quote | 3 | 0 ... True quote data lives in OrderHeader').
anomalies.recommended_action: Encode in ETL and M9 sync mappers: quote extraction filters OrderHeader by OrderType; QuoteRank/ItemQuoteStatus crosswalk as lookups only.

anomalies.finding: Hire subsystem (3 tables) is empty, no equipment-rental business in BisTrack; out of Phase 1 scope.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory Subsystem Summary ('Hire | 3 | 0').
anomalies.recommended_action: Exclude; one-line confirmation with Dibbits that no rental line of business is planned for go-live.

anomalies.finding: Version-suffixed table cruft beyond the BAK table: ProductPriceHistory2, SalesAnalysis2 AND SalesAnalysis3 coexist (170K and 167K rows), superseded copies likely linger, and the authoritative version per family is unproven.
anomalies.evidence: SchemaInventory All Tables rows 5, 11, 16.
anomalies.recommended_action: During the BT-A-009 triage pass, identify base/older versions (ProductPriceHistory without suffix? SalesAnalysis 1?) and prove which copy current BisTrack code writes to (proc references) before using any as a migration or velocity-seed source.

anomalies.finding: Doc drift across the sync spec lineage: the bistrack sync migration is numbered 053 (M9 §04), 055 (ARCHITECTURE.md), and 074 (applied per M9 §07); sync cadence is 'every 5 minutes' in ARCHITECTURE §2.3 vs the 15-minute floor in M9 NFRs; the Go module exists only in the old fork and is not yet ported.
anomalies.evidence: m9-bistrack-sync.md §04 migrations table, §07 ('Migration 074... applied (schema only)'; module port pending); ARCHITECTURE.md §2.3 + §3.1 (055_bistrack_sync.sql).
